PRESUMPTION-317:
  Date surfaced: 2026-06-07
  Statement: [inferred] The original weekly-task design presumed that the scheduled-task execution environment is the same, capability-uniform "agent" as the attended Cowork environment — i.e., that "the agent can do X here" implies "the agent can do X on a schedule." The push/worktree design only makes sense if scheduled tasks inherit Tom's Mac (credentials, normal `$HOME`, writable `.git`). The whole category of "two distinct execution contexts with different capabilities" was never modeled until the trial run forced it into view.
  Evidence it was operative: the task was built to push via a git worktree and to read `$HOME/Documents/...` paths; both presuppose an attended-Mac environment. The failure ("they run in this same sandbox that can't push, can't resolve `$HOME`, and can't touch `.git` locks") is the negation of an unstated uniformity premise.
  Why it was unstated: too foundational to notice — "the agent" is experienced as one actor, so the possibility that its scheduled self runs in a strictly weaker sandbox was invisible until empirically hit.
  Type: structural
  Related decisions: DECISION-052
  Related assumptions: ASSUMPTION-285 (the corrected, grounded capability model), ASSUMPTION-286 (the policy/capability layering this blind spot made visible)
  Related presumptions: PRESUMPTION-318 (build-before-probe), PRESUMPTION-320 (blind command blocks)
  Testability: testable via literature (multi-environment / heterogeneous-runtime agent deployment; the gap between interactive and batch/scheduled execution contexts; capability discovery before action)
  Risk if wrong: High — every present or future scheduled task that silently assumes attended-context capabilities (push, credentialed APIs, `$HOME`, lock mutation) will fail or, worse, half-complete and leave cruft, exactly as happened here. This is a class bug, not a one-off.
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:
    Origin: 14b
    Chain: [14b]
    Original item: PRESUMPTION-317
    Item type: PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference)
    Transform at each step:
      14b: Surfaced as the unstated uniformity premise beneath the mistaken push design; the negative space that ASSUMPTION-285 fills once stated. The day's strongest fail-loud item (High); pairs ASSUMPTION-285. Routed HIGH.
    Current status: UNTESTED

  Evidence it was operative: the task was created and a memory note written ("the connectome is now auto-maintained") before the trial run revealed the push was impossible; the scheduled agent had to discover the constraint by running into it ("memory suggests it can't … let me check whether the sandbox can actually push"). The two subsequent half-failed command blocks are downstream of the same build-then-discover ordering.
  Why it was unstated: methodological habit — environment capabilities are assumed stable and known, so "can this run here?" is not posed as a precondition the way code correctness is.
  Type: methodological
  Related decisions: DECISION-052
  Related assumptions: ASSUMPTION-283 (the scheduling remedy), ASSUMPTION-285 (the capability model arrived at only after the failure)
  Related presumptions: PRESUMPTION-317 (the uniformity premise this build-order presumed)

  Risk if wrong: Medium — recurring build-before-probe ordering produces avoidable rework and, when the failing step mutates shared state (here `.git` locks), real collateral cost. Self-referential: C2A2's own build violated its constitution's caution-over-speed bias.
  Status: UNTESTED

  Statement: [inferred] The "approved data auto-publishes, code is gated" guard (ASSUMPTION-284) presumes that PRS-data regeneration is deterministic and epistemically safe enough to push to the live viz with no human eyes — that a count change like 231 → 269 carries no interpretive risk worth reviewing. New triplets entering the published connectome unreviewed is itself a publish-without-review path, but it is treated as categorically different from a code change rather than as a (smaller) instance of the same risk.
  Evidence it was operative: the guard draws the review boundary exclusively at generator/template changes; the data delta is waved through ("approved-PRS data auto-publishes"). The word "approved" does the load-bearing work, but what makes a freshly-extracted triplet "approved" enough to skip visual review is never specified.
  Why it was unstated: the data/code line feels self-evidently safe — data is "just the numbers" — so the assumption that data changes never need visual review goes unexamined.
  Type: normative / epistemic
  Related decisions: DECISION-052
  Related assumptions: ASSUMPTION-284 (the data/code split whose data half this examines)
  Related presumptions: PRESUMPTION-317 (the environment that ultimately made even the data auto-push impossible, deferring the question rather than resolving it)
  Testability: testable via literature (risk classification of data vs code changes in automated publishing; when derived-data updates warrant human review; silent data-quality regressions)
  Risk if wrong: Medium — if a bad or mis-extracted triplet can reach the public connectome unreviewed, the "approved data is safe" line lets a data-quality regression publish silently; the manual-push fallback currently masks this, but the design intent still treats data as review-exempt.

PRESUMPTION-320:
  Date surfaced: 2026-06-07
  Statement: [inferred] Repeatedly handing Tom multi-command shell blocks to paste-run presumed those blocks would execute atomically and as-modeled on his machine — i.e., that the agent's model of the user's repo state (branch, staged files, worktree registrations, lock files) is accurate enough to script blind, multi-step, state-mutating sequences. Two of the three blocks half-failed precisely because the real state diverged from the model (a locked stale worktree still holding `main`; `generate_community_explorer.py` already staged).
  Evidence it was operative: block #1 aborted mid-sequence (`'main' is already used by worktree …`; then committed on the wrong branch, bundling a stray staged file); only block #3, rewritten to use a throwaway detached worktree built straight from `origin/main` (assuming nothing about local state), succeeded. The progression from state-dependent to state-independent blocks is the tell that the earlier ones over-trusted the state model.
  Why it was unstated: convenience framing — a pasteable block reads as a single safe action, so the compound risk of several state-dependent steps running non-atomically on a possibly-divergent repo is not surfaced to the user.
  Type: methodological
  Related decisions: DECISION-052
  Related assumptions: ASSUMPTION-285 (sandbox can't run the git itself, forcing the hand-off-to-Tom pattern that produced the blocks)
  Related presumptions: PRESUMPTION-317, PRESUMPTION-318
  Testability: testable via literature (risk of blind/compound remote command execution; idempotent vs state-dependent operations; human-in-the-loop ops where the operator can't see intermediate state; "make each step safe to fail")
  Risk if wrong: Medium-High — a state-divergent multi-command block can cause real damage on the user's machine (here: an accidental commit on the wrong branch plus stale `.git` locks that briefly jammed Tom's git); the cost lands on the user, not the sandbox.
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:
    Origin: 14b
    Chain: [14b]
    Original item: PRESUMPTION-320
    Item type: PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference)
    Transform at each step:

    Current status: UNTESTED

## 2026-06-08 — 14b EOD batch (attended OpenStory → Agent Explorer build day; 4 sessions)

*Surfaced from the same four 2026-06-08 attended sessions read by 14a (handoff notes `HANDOFF_openstory_{c2a2,session2,session3,session4}.md` + described artifacts). 6 PRESUMPTIONs (322-327). Dedup check against today's 14a items (287-292): non-overlapping — 287-292 are the stated design rationales; 322-327 are the unexamined premises beneath them. Pairings noted per item.*

PRESUMPTION-322:
  Date surfaced: 2026-06-08
  Statement: [inferred] The build presumes the OpenStory event stream is a *faithful* proxy for what an agent is and does — that counts, durations, eval/apply, and tool-use adequately capture an agent's substance. The Explorer re-bases each agent's self-representation from its constitutional markdown (authored intent) onto its observed telemetry (ASSUMPTION-287), but never asks what the trace *misses*: an agent can emit many events and little value, or few events and decisive judgment. The qualitative content of a tradition-agent's contribution is presumed to survive reduction to a behavioral fingerprint.
  Evidence it was operative: every per-agent statistic in `agent_telemetry.json` (sessions, events, eval/apply, tool_coverage, durations) is treated as the agent's profile; the detail panel renders telemetry as the agent's reality; nowhere in the four sessions is the adequacy of telemetry-as-proxy questioned — only its accuracy (reconciliation against SQL) and completeness (capture gap) are.
  Why it was unstated: too foundational to notice — observability culture treats "what was logged" as "what happened"; the move from authored intent to observed behavior was framed as a strict upgrade ("replaces it with observed telemetry"), so the proxy gap was invisible.
  Type: structural / epistemic
  Related decisions: DECISION-053
  Related assumptions: ASSUMPTION-287, ASSUMPTION-288
  Testability: testable via literature (observability/telemetry as proxy for purpose; trace-vs-intent gap; what behavioral metrics systematically omit about agent quality)
  Risk if wrong: Medium-High — if telemetry is a lossy proxy, the Explorer (and any downstream judgment built on it) will mistake activity for substance, privileging legible/busy agents over quiet/decisive ones, and degrade exactly the self-knowledge the self-awareness layer exists to provide.
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:
    Origin: 14b
    Chain: [14b]
    Original item: PRESUMPTION-322

PRESUMPTION-326:
  Date surfaced: 2026-06-08
  Statement: [inferred] The ingest design presumes recent / available activity is representative of an agent — the bounded 72h restart window (chosen to keep restart cost constant) plus the decision to build on the existing DB rather than reseed (ASSUMPTION-292) plus the sparse pre-tool-field history (`tool_coverage≈0` for older sessions) together mean the Explorer structurally over-renders high-frequency, recently-active agents and under-renders low-frequency ones. The slow tradition-agents the project most cares about are precisely the ones whose tool maps stay "sparse until fresh runs land."
  Evidence it was operative: HANDOFF-2 "bounded 72h window … restarts are constant-cost"; HANDOFF-3 caveat "`tool_coverage` … older (pre-tool-field) sessions read 0, so thinker-agent tool maps are sparse until fresh runs land"; ASSUMPTION-292's "build on the current DB" defers the full backfill that would fill the tail.
  Why it was unstated: an engineering optimization (constant-cost restarts; don't perturb serve) whose representational side effect — a recency/availability bias in what the Explorer shows — was never weighed against the optimization.
  Type: scaling
  Related decisions: DECISION-053
  Related assumptions: ASSUMPTION-290, ASSUMPTION-292
  Related open questions: OPEN-078
  Testability: testable empirically (capture completeness vs agent run-frequency) / literature (recency and survivorship bias in windowed log analytics; sampling bias in observability)
  Risk if wrong: Medium-High — a tool meant to reveal the whole swarm would instead foreground busy/recent agents and dim the quiet, slow, or weekly ones, inverting the project's actual priorities (tradition depth over operational throughput) and giving a misleading account of which agents are "active."
  Status: UNTESTED

PRESUMPTION-355:
  Date surfaced: 2026-06-16
  Statement: [inferred] The epistemically meaningful event in a PRS triplet's life is its CREATION (first git appearance), not its later revision, validation, use, or retirement — the yield metric counts births and never counts maturation or death. A triplet drafted and committed once weighs the same as one that was reworked across months or that proved load-bearing for a cross-connection; a retired triplet still counts as yield. The "metabolism" of the system is thereby modeled as a birth-rate, not a throughput or a survival process.
  Evidence it was operative: `prs_yield.py` records only first-appearance dates and a flat per-day count; there is no revision-weight, quality-weight, or survival term. Retired ids are kept in the cumulative (ASSUMPTION-324). No part of the build discussed counting anything other than first appearances.
  Why it was unstated: too foundational to notice — "production" reads as self-evidently the thing to count when building a yield metric, so the choice to equate yield with first-creation (rather than with maturation or sustained use) was never posed as a choice.
  Type: epistemic / methodological
  Related decisions: DECISION-059; DECISION-058
  Related items: ASSUMPTION-322 (first-appearance production); ASSUMPTION-318 (files-added headline — same births-not-throughput shape); PRESUMPTION-349 (file-count commensurability); PRESUMPTION-350 (commit-as-clock)
  Testability: testable empirically (do first-appearance counts correlate with independently-rated research progress better or worse than revision-weighted or survival-weighted alternatives?) and via literature (creation-event vs. lifecycle metrics in scientometrics / software-evolution)
  Risk if wrong: Medium — a birth-rate metric can show healthy "yield" while the corpus is churning, stagnating in quality, or shedding mass; the metabolism story it tells could be systematically optimistic.
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:
    Origin: 14b
    Chain: [14b]
    Original item: PRESUMPTION-355
    Item type: PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference)
    Transform at each step:
      14b: Inferred from the structure of `prs_yield.py` (first-appearance-only, unweighted, retired-ids-retained). High-confidence that creation is the only event counted; the normative reading (births ≠ health) surfaced neutrally. [inferred]
    Current status: UNTESTED

  Risk if wrong: Medium — if the "resolved" framing closes the sequencing question prematurely, the view layer hardens around numbers before their premises are tested, and the authority halo makes later correction costlier (the same dynamic OPEN-083 already warns about for the metabolism cliff).

  Risk if wrong: Medium-High — load-bearing for whether synthesis coverage is actually complete; if true synthesis demand is undercounted by the broken-link proxy, the vault can look "substantially built out (45 synthesis pages, bridges resolving)" while missing the bridges that matter most, and the all-clear is circular.
  Status: UNTESTED

PRESUMPTION-385:

  Statement: [inferred] That "one agent per thinker" is the right unit at which to add redundancy and voting. Pathway 31 makes the per-thinker assessment the thing to triple; it does not ask whether the locus where robustness matters most is instead the cross-tradition EDGE, the PRS-triplet, or the synthesis claim. The whole architecture inherits the existing one-agent-per-thinker decomposition as the frame.
  Evidence it was operative: "Today the system runs one agent per thinker … Pathway 31 replaces the single assessor with three independent column agents" — the unit is taken as given; alternatives at other granularities are never raised.
  Why it was unstated: too foundational to notice (the per-thinker unit predates this pathway)
  Type: structural
  Related decisions: DECISION-062
  Testability: testable via literature — ensemble/redundancy placement in multi-agent systems; where voting adds value vs where it is wasted
  Risk if wrong: Medium — effort triples the assessment that may not be the fragile joint
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:

    Original item: PRESUMPTION-385

PRESUMPTION-386:
  Date surfaced: 2026-06-24
  Statement: [inferred] That semantic agreement among 2-of-3 differently-wired columns tracks CORRECTNESS, not merely shared bias. Even with different corpus slices and analytic axes, all three columns are likely the same base model family reading the same thinker's material; their convergence could be consensus-on-error (correlated model priors), which a vote cannot detect and would in fact launder into false confidence.
  Evidence it was operative: the design treats 2-of-3 agreement as the trustworthy output ("the adjudicator emits the agreed assessment") and dissensus as the only flagged state — agreement is presumed to be the safe case.
  Why it was unstated: obvious-seeming (voting-implies-reliability intuition); the redundancy trap is named for VARIANCE but not for correlated BIAS
  Type: epistemic
  Related decisions: DECISION-062
  Related items: ASSUMPTION-347 (independence axes address variance, not necessarily shared bias)
  Testability: testable via literature — correlated-error / shared-bias failure of ensembles and majority voting; diversity vs accuracy in model ensembles
  Risk if wrong: High — a confident consensus assessment that is wrong is worse than a single-agent assessment flagged as uncertain
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:
    Origin: 14b
    Chain: [14b]
    Original item: PRESUMPTION-386
    Item type: PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference)
    Transform at each step:
      14b: Inferred from the gap between the stated variance-trap (ASSUMPTION-347) and the unaddressed correlated-bias case. [inferred, high-confidence]
    Current status: UNTESTED

PRESUMPTION-446:

  Evidence it was operative: lock collisions are handled as recurring weather ("matches the recurring pattern") rather than as a design gap; no session has proposed a coordination mechanism.

  Testability: testable via literature (concurrency control for shared mutable stores; multi-agent resource coordination) and empirically (map all writers' schedules against observed lock events).

The race was in fact lost in one respect — the daily agent committed review_log.html first — and the outcome was salvaged by luck of convergence, not by the mechanism.
  Why it was unstated: culturally embedded — optimistic concurrency is the default habit of solo developers; the repo's transition to a multi-writer system happened gradually and the coordination question was explicitly parked (DECISION-077, post-ISME).

PRESUMPTION-457:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-07
  Statement: [inferred] That the model's training-data knowledge of a thinker's appearance catalog is a valid oracle for adjudicating live web-search results — when search says "new episode" and the prior says "no such episode," the prior wins.
  Evidence it was operative: the Hoffman agent rejected the "Lex Fridman June 2026" result on the ground that "the only real Lex/Hoffman episode is #293 from June 2022" — a claim about 2026 events sourced from the model's memory, which cannot contain them. The rejection was likely correct here (the accepted StarTalk item got two confirming searches; the rejected one got none targeted at proving it real), but the asymmetry — extra verification effort spent on the item the prior favored, summary dismissal of the one it disfavored — went unexamined. A real post-cutoff Lex episode would be filtered out by exactly this rule.
  Why it was unstated: too foundational to notice — using what the model "knows" as the baseline for plausibility is the default reasoning mode; the direction of the burden of proof was never chosen, only inherited.

  Related decisions: none on record
  Related items: ASSUMPTION-426 (the stated half of this behavior); PRESUMPTION-442 lineage (metric/evidence-interpretation presumptions)
  Testability: testable via literature — hallucination-vs-novelty discrimination in retrieval-augmented systems; calibration of prior-vs-evidence weighting when evidence postdates training. Testable empirically — false-rejection audit of catalog-prior filtering (ASSUMPTION-426's test covers both).
  Risk if wrong: Medium — tradition agents systematically under-capture genuinely new appearances, which is the one job the ~30-day window exists for; misses are invisible (nothing audits rejected candidates).
  Status: CHALLENGED (REVISE-191 via DISPOSITION-429, 2026-07-09 — verification rule: prior is not oracle post-cutoff)
  Provenance:

PRESUMPTION-480:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-13
  Statement: [inferred] Captured work is presumed non-perishable. The proposal inbox holds 24 items pending since 2026-07-01 — and the wiki agent filed 4 more today — with no expiry, no decay, no triage, and no policy that treats a capture's value as a function of latency. The system's producers are throttled by nothing and its consumer is absent; the design presumes the queue simply waits.
  Evidence it was operative: The morning handoff reports "24 pending items going back to 2026-07-01 — the backlog has been growing for twelve days with no [C2A2-review-decision] email to clear it," and the same day's c282-wiki-agent run added 4 more proposals without reference to the backlog's depth. No artifact anywhere in the architecture assigns a proposal an age, a half-life, or a shed condition; ~29 REVISE flags now pool in the same way for the same absent reviewer.
  Why it was unstated: culturally embedded — an append-only registry is the system's native form, and append-only artifacts have no vocabulary for staleness; the wiki's value proposition (nothing is lost) quietly implies that nothing degrades
  Type: normative (with a methodological component: no triage rule)
  Related decisions: none — REVISE-210 (operator-absence quiescence) proposes throttling *production*; this concerns the *perishability of what is already produced*, which quiescence would not address
  Related items: OPEN-115, OPEN-116 (backlog and cadence); ASSUMPTION-430 (priority-ordered partial burn); the aging-queue priority-decay presumption already CHALLENGED in the 15d family; ASSUMPTION-428 (escalation clock, expired, discharging into a down channel)
  Testability: testable via literature — queueing under abandonment, perishable-inventory and freshness-decay models, the software-engineering evidence on stale-issue/PR-rot; testable empirically — re-score a sample of the 24 pending proposals against their filing-day rationale and measure how many are now moot, superseded, or contradicted by later captures.
  Risk if wrong: Medium — if proposals do perish, the backlog is not a debt but a loss already taken, and the review session Tom is being asked to schedule is partly archaeology; the priority list handed to him each morning would then be ordered by filing date rather than by remaining value.
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:
    Origin: 14b
    Chain: [14b]
    Original item: PRESUMPTION-480
    Item type: PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference)
    Transform at each step:
      14b: Inferred from the co-occurrence of a 13-day-old unreviewed backlog, same-day unthrottled production into it, and the absence of any decay/triage vocabulary anywhere in the architecture; moderate-to-high confidence. Distinguished from REVISE-210 (which throttles production) and from the 15d priority-decay item (which concerns rank churn in the lit-search re-trigger queue, not proposal perishability). [inferred]
    Current status: UNTESTED

PRESUMPTION-481:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-14
  Statement: [inferred] A scheduled task that crashes mid-run is presumed to be a harmless no-op — as if it "didn't happen" and will be covered by tomorrow's run. Today four tasks (c2a2-lit-search-pipeline, evening cowork→chat, morning walk handoff, deferred-action monitor) each fired and then died with "API Error: Connection closed mid-response." None retried, none emitted a partial artifact, none raised an alarm, and none left a trace in any registry. The architecture presumes runs are idempotent and losslessly skippable.
  Evidence it was operative: The lit-search pipeline crashed after two WebSearches, so lit_search_returns.md has no 2026-07-14 section at all — a whole day's epistemic throughput vanished with no record that it was attempted. The evening sync crashed before writing its primary .md (see ASSUMPTION-458). Yet nothing in the fleet reacts to a crash: there is no retry policy, no partial-output checkpoint, and no "this task started but did not finish" signal anywhere. The watchdog, reading only lastRunAt, called the day healthy (ASSUMPTION-456).
  Why it was unstated: too foundational to notice — the scheduler's mental model is "fire on cron," and a fired task is assumed to run to completion or to fail visibly; mid-response infrastructure crashes were not in the design's failure vocabulary, which until 07-13 held only login-outage and (07-13) quota-exhaustion.
  Type: structural (with a methodological component: no retry/checkpoint/alarm on partial failure)
  Related decisions: none
  Related items: ASSUMPTION-456 (watchdog health criterion blind to mid-run crashes); ASSUMPTION-458 (.md fallback defeated by pre-Step-2 crash); PRESUMPTION-479 (failure modes not mutually exclusive — connection-crash is now a third coexisting cause); OPEN-119 (quota); OPEN-120 (today, the retry/alarm policy)
  Testability: framework/architectural for the "harmless no-op" presumption itself; the reliability sub-claim is testable empirically — measure the mid-response crash rate of the fleet's runs over a window, and whether crashed runs are recovered by the next scheduled fire or silently lost.
  Risk if wrong: High — if crashed runs are not harmless, the pipeline loses days of work invisibly; today the self-awareness pipeline's own upstream (the lit-search returns it consumes) produced nothing, and no instrument noticed. A loss that leaves no trace cannot be prioritised, and the watchdog actively certifies it as health.
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:
    Origin: 14b
    Chain: [14b]
    Original item: PRESUMPTION-481
    Item type: PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference)
    Transform at each step:
      14b: Inferred from four same-day mid-response crashes (read directly in their transcripts) set against the absence of any retry, checkpoint, alarm, or registry trace, and the watchdog's all-clear; high confidence. Checked against 14a: ASSUMPTION-456 records the watchdog's blindness to the symptom; this records the presumed harmlessness beneath it. [inferred]
    Current status: UNTESTED

PRESUMPTION-482:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-14
  Statement: [inferred] The self-awareness pipeline presumes it can fully observe the day it audits — that the transcripts it can read are the transcripts that matter. 14a/14b run at end-of-day and reason over whatever session records exist; today four of the day's runs crashed mid-response, so the audited record is materially incomplete, yet the pipeline has no measure of its own observational completeness and no way to register "N runs are missing from what I can see."
  Evidence it was operative: This very run reconstructs 2026-07-14 from the transcripts that survived (scheduler health, project status, system health, the wiki agent's proposals) plus wiki artifacts, while four crashed runs left only a truncated "Connection closed" tail and no output. The changelog will describe the day as if the surviving records are the day; nothing in 14a's or 14b's definition asks "what fraction of today's runs am I unable to read, and how does that bound my conclusions?"
  Why it was unstated: culturally embedded — the pipeline was designed for a world where sessions complete and produce transcripts; incompleteness of the audit record is not a failure mode the auditor was built to detect, so its coverage is presumed total by default.
  Type: epistemic
  Related decisions: none
  Related items: PRESUMPTION-481 (crash-as-no-op — the mechanism that produces the missing records); ASSUMPTION-456 (the watchdog's parallel blind spot at the monitoring layer); the SYSTEMIC-RISK self-certification family (A-452 — an auditor that cannot see its own coverage gaps is a kind of self-certification)
  Testability: testable empirically — cross-check the set of scheduled fires expected on a given day (from the scheduler spec) against the set the pipeline actually read; the difference is the pipeline's blind fraction and can be reported as a completeness metric.
  Risk if wrong: Medium-High — if the audited record is routinely incomplete, the daily changelog and metrics silently overstate their own coverage, and the self-awareness system inherits exactly the firing-health blindness it was built to catch in others.
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:
    Origin: 14b
    Chain: [14b]
    Original item: PRESUMPTION-482
    Item type: PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference)
    Transform at each step:
      14b: Inferred from the gap between the day's expected runs and the runs this pipeline could actually read, given four crashes; moderate-to-high confidence. Distinguished from PRESUMPTION-481 (which concerns the crashed tasks) — this concerns the auditor's unmeasured coverage of them. [inferred]
    Current status: UNTESTED

PRESUMPTION-483:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-14
  Statement: [inferred] Two monitors agreeing is presumed to be stronger evidence than one — monitoring redundancy is presumed to increase reliability. Today both the scheduler health check and the morning project status independently reported "all clear / nothing overdue," which reads as corroboration; but both verdicts rest on the same firing/lastRunAt signal, so their agreement is one blind spot counted twice, not two independent confirmations.
  Evidence it was operative: Scheduler health: "37 enabled tasks, all running on schedule ... Action needed: None." Morning project status: "About thirty scheduled tasks are active and nothing is overdue ... all ran clean overnight." Neither verified output artifacts for the four tasks that crashed mid-response; both derive "healthy" from the same lastRunAt-based criterion. The morning system-health agent, which does read artifacts, is the only monitor that surfaced real failures (OpenStory down 9 days, metabolism freshness) — and it disagreed with the other two.
  Why it was unstated: obvious-to-participants / culturally embedded — having several monitors feels safer than having one, and the design never asked whether the monitors are independent; correlated instruments look like redundancy until they fail together.
  Type: epistemic (with a methodological component: no independence check across monitors)
  Related decisions: none
  Related items: ASSUMPTION-456 (the shared criterion); the SYSTEMIC-RISK self-certification family and ASSUMPTION-452 (no self-produced artifact may certify itself — correlated green checks are a soft form of it); PRESUMPTION-481, PRESUMPTION-482
  Testability: testable empirically — map each monitor to the signal it consumes; two monitors reading the same lastRunAt field have zero added coverage, which a one-page dependency audit establishes. Testable via literature — common-cause failure and independence assumptions in redundant monitoring (N-version programming, correlated-failure results).
  Risk if wrong: Medium — if agreement among correlated monitors is being read as corroboration, the fleet's apparent monitoring depth is illusory, and adding more same-signal monitors raises confidence without raising coverage; the one monitor that reads artifacts (system health) gets outvoted by two that do not.
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:
    Origin: 14b
    Chain: [14b]
    Original item: PRESUMPTION-483
    Item type: PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference)
    Transform at each step:
      14b: Inferred from two same-signal monitors reporting all-clear while a third artifact-reading monitor found real failures; moderate confidence. Checked against 14a: ASSUMPTION-456 captures the shared criterion; this captures the presumed independence of the monitors built on it. [inferred]
    Current status: UNTESTED

PRESUMPTION-484:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-15
  Statement: [inferred] A flag or watch is presumed to reflect current evidence — once FINDING-048 (embedding-space ≡ FEP) is set as a live paradigm-shift watch under FLAG-016, it is treated as standing on present data, when in fact a flag is a snapshot that can silently detach from the evidence stream meant to confirm or kill it. The design presumes flags are self-refreshing; nothing couples a watch's status to the freshness of the ingestion path beneath it.
  Evidence it was operative: The 2026-07-15 handoff notes the heavy Levin batch that FEEDS FINDING-048 is un-ingested (master wiki silent since 07-09), yet the watch is still reported as one of the 6 active flagged/paradigm-shift-watch items with no staleness marker and no adjustment to its standing. The system carries the flag forward as if its evidence base were current; there is no field anywhere that reads "the deposits relevant to this flag are 5 days behind."
  Why it was unstated: too foundational to notice — a flag feels like a live property of the network, not a timestamped claim about a data state; the ingestion path between deposits and findings is invisible in the flag's own representation, so its lag is not something the watch is built to see.
  Type: epistemic (with a methodological component: no coupling between a finding's status and its upstream evidence freshness)
  Related decisions: none
  Related items: ASSUMPTION-460 (the stated ingestion-consequence claim), ASSUMPTION-455 (master stale since 07-09); PRESUMPTION-480 (captured work presumed non-perishable — kin: a flag is a capture that can go stale); OPEN-120 (today); the firing-health family
  Testability: testable empirically — in-house: trace FINDING-048's evidence base to the un-ingested deposits and show whether its confirm/kill condition is currently computable at all. Testable via literature — alert/monitor staleness, stale-while-revalidate and cache-coherence reasoning, and the epistemology of "watch" states that outlive their evidence window.
  Risk if wrong: High — if flags are read as current when their evidence is frozen, the paradigm-shift channel (C2A2's central evidence stream) can carry a watch that is neither confirmed nor killed but merely stalled, and a downstream reader cannot tell the difference between "still open on live data" and "open because the data stopped arriving."
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:
    Origin: 14b
    Chain: [14b]
    Original item: PRESUMPTION-484
    Item type: PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference)
    Transform at each step:
      14b: Inferred from a live flagged watch (FINDING-048/FLAG-016) carried forward with no staleness signal while its feeding deposits are un-ingested; high confidence on the coupling gap. Checked against 14a: ASSUMPTION-460 states the ingestion consequence; this surfaces the unstated presumption that flags self-refresh. [inferred]
    Current status: UNTESTED

PRESUMPTION-485:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-15
  Statement: [inferred] The architecture presumes the set of failure causes is closed and enumerable — each newly observed cause is treated as completing the taxonomy rather than as one draw from an open population. The failure vocabulary has grown login-outage → quota-exhaustion (07-13) → ConnectionRefused / mid-response crash (07-14, 07-15), and every remedy queued so far is a point-fix aimed at the last named cause; the presumption that the list is now complete is what lets a bounded remedy set be treated as sufficient.
  Evidence it was operative: The queued remedies REVISE-198 (Gmail fallback) and REVISE-199 (ack + escalation) both presuppose the failing channel can still transmit — they answer the login-outage and were defeated first by quota (a channel that produces nothing) and again today by ConnectionRefused (a channel that never connects). No item in the family reserves room for "a cause we have not yet seen"; each new signature is absorbed as the final one. The morning project status still reported the fleet all-clear the same day a producer crashed on an unmodeled cause.
  Why it was unstated: culturally embedded — debugging proceeds cause-by-cause, and finding a concrete cause feels like finding the cause; an open-world stance ("there are failure modes we have not enumerated and our fixes must degrade gracefully against them") is not the default posture of a point-fix workflow.
  Type: epistemic (with a methodological component: remedies target named causes rather than failure classes)
  Related decisions: none
  Related items: ASSUMPTION-444 (sync-outage single-cause, CONTESTED), ASSUMPTION-461 (today — the third failure signature), PRESUMPTION-479 (causes not mutually exclusive — kin: 479 says they co-occur, 485 says the set is unbounded), PRESUMPTION-481 (mid-run crash), REVISE-198/199
  Testability: testable via literature — open-world vs. closed-world failure analysis, unknown-unknowns and the limits of root-cause enumeration, resilience-engineering critiques of exhaustive-cause reasoning (the Cook doctrine already cited in DISPOSITION-458), and graceful-degradation / defense-in-depth as the open-world alternative. Testable empirically — count how many distinct failure signatures have appeared since 07-01 and how many queued remedies each subsequent signature defeated.
  Risk if wrong: Medium — if the failure population is open but treated as closed, the fleet keeps shipping remedies that the next unmodeled cause defeats, spending effort on point-fixes while the delivery channel stays down; the correct posture (degrade gracefully against unknown causes) is never adopted because the list always looks one fix from complete.
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:
    Origin: 14b
    Chain: [14b]
    Original item: PRESUMPTION-485
    Item type: PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference)
    Transform at each step:
      14b: Inferred from a growing failure vocabulary (login → quota → connection errors) met by point-fix remedies each defeated by the next cause; moderate-high confidence. Checked against 14a: ASSUMPTION-461 states the third signature as fact; this surfaces the unstated presumption that the cause list is closed. Distinct from PRESUMPTION-479 (co-occurrence) — this is about the openness of the set. [inferred]
    Current status: UNTESTED

PRESUMPTION-486:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-16
  Statement: [inferred] Re-syncing the master-wiki narrative "Current status" line is presumed to discharge the staleness concern raised by ASSUMPTION-455/460 — but narrative-freshness and evidence-freshness are decoupled. The c282 run advanced the status line to 07-16 (flagging the 07-10→07-15 gap) while adding zero triplets; the network stayed frozen at 300/90/50. The fix touched the indicator, not the referent: the pointer now reads current while the deposits feeding FINDING-048 remain un-ingested. A reader who trusts the status line will now believe the ingestion is caught up when it is not.
  Evidence it was operative: the run logged "master narrative re-synced" as a completed cleanup step (Phase 5) and reported the network unchanged in the same breath (Phase 1: no triplets; "frozen ... two weeks"), treating the narrative repair as the resolution of the flagged gap without noting that the evidence path is untouched.
  Why it was unstated: too foundational to notice — the status line is habitually read as the system's freshness signal, so refreshing it feels like refreshing the state.
  Type: epistemic
  Related decisions: none
  Related items: ASSUMPTION-462 (the stated re-sync), ASSUMPTION-460 / PRESUMPTION-484 (staleness starves FINDING-048), OPEN-120 (evidence-freshness gate)
  Testability: testable empirically — in-house: diff the master wiki's "Current status" date against the mtime/last-ingested-deposit of its network-state block; show the two now disagree (status 07-16, evidence 07-01/07-09). Literature: indicator/referent decoupling, "green dashboard over stale data," Goodhart-style substitution of the freshness signal for freshness.
  Risk if wrong: High — a refreshed pointer over frozen evidence actively conceals the very staleness A-455/460 flagged, making the stalled paradigm-shift watch harder to detect, not easier.
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:
    Origin: 14b
    Chain: [14b]
    Original item: PRESUMPTION-486
    Item type: PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference)
    Transform at each step:
      14b: Inferred from the 2026-07-16 c282 daily-run transcript — the narrative re-sync logged as cleanup alongside an explicit "no triplets added / frozen two weeks." [inferred, high-confidence]
    Current status: UNTESTED

PRESUMPTION-487:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-16
  Statement: [inferred] The No-Blind-Push governance rule and the daily "leave it staged for the Mac" resolution presume a human will regularly appear at the Mac to review and push staged work. The safety rule is safe only if the bottleneck it creates is actually staffed; on an 11-day autonomous stretch with no attended session, "staged for the Mac" is functionally equivalent to "never persisted." The rule was designed for a cadence of human attention that the current operating reality does not supply, so a safety mechanism has quietly become a durability failure.
  Evidence it was operative: the run invoked No-Blind-Push and stopped at "staged," treating that as a safe terminal state — with no signal about how long staged work may sit, no staging-age alarm, and no fallback path, exactly as if a same-day human review were assumed.
  Why it was unstated: culturally embedded — the fleet's constitution was written assuming an attending operator, so the operator's presence is a background premise no individual run re-examines.
  Type: structural (with a scaling component: the human-review step does not scale to N autonomous days)
  Related decisions: none (rests on the No-Blind-Push constitutional rule)
  Related items: ASSUMPTION-463 (git-persistence cannot self-complete), OPEN-121 (who closes the persistence loop), PRESUMPTION-480 (perishability of unattended work), the review-backlog-26 / 15-day-gap (same absent-human premise on the approval side)
  Testability: testable empirically — in-house: measure the age of the oldest staged-but-uncommitted change set and the interval since the last human push; if either exceeds the run cadence, the presumed review is not occurring. Literature: human-in-the-loop bottlenecks, safety interlocks that fail-closed into unavailability, queueing without a consumer.
  Risk if wrong: High — every autonomous run's durable output depends on a human step that has been absent 11 days; a safety rule is silently discarding work it believes it is protecting.
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:
    Origin: 14b
    Chain: [14b]
    Original item: PRESUMPTION-487
    Item type: PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference)
    Transform at each step:
      14b: Inferred from the 2026-07-16 c282 Phase 6 assessment set against the 11-day autonomous streak (no attended session in any 07-16 transcript). [inferred, high-confidence]
    Current status: UNTESTED

PRESUMPTION-488:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-16
  Statement: [inferred] Each monitoring agent presumes "healthy" is a property of the system rather than of its own vantage. Morning project status reads OpenStory-healthy from a live DB probe; evening cowork→chat reads OpenStory-down from the delivery/usability vantage — both on 2026-07-16. Neither is wrong from where it stands; the fleet presumes any single agent's verdict generalizes to "the subsystem's health," and it has no reconciler that would even notice two agents issuing contradictory same-day verdicts on the same subsystem. Health is treated as global and singular when it is actually vantage-relative and plural.
  Evidence it was operative: the morning run emitted an unqualified "No issues to report" and "database is healthy"; the evening run emitted "down an 11th day" — and nothing in the fleet flags the contradiction. Each verdict is stated as if it were the subsystem's state, not the observer's slice of it.
  Why it was unstated: obvious to each participant from within its own probe — a live DB genuinely looks healthy to a DB probe; the vantage-dependence only appears when two verdicts are laid side by side, which no run does.
  Type: epistemic (with a methodological component: no cross-agent reconciliation step exists)
  Related decisions: none
  Related items: ASSUMPTION-464 (the stated contradiction), ASSUMPTION-456 (firing ≠ valid output), SYSTEMIC-RISK #4 LIVENESS-AS-SUCCESS, PRESUMPTION-483 (correlated green checks — the inverse case: agreement counted twice; here disagreement noticed zero times)
  Testability: testable empirically — in-house: for each subsystem, enumerate which agents report on it and which signal each consumes; detect and surface same-day verdict disagreements automatically. Literature: partial observability and vantage-relative health; the difference between "process up," "data fresh," and "service usable"; multi-observer state reconciliation.
  Risk if wrong: Medium-High — a subsystem can be simultaneously certified healthy and reported dead with neither verdict escalated, so real outages hide behind a truthful-from-somewhere green.
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:
    Origin: 14b
    Chain: [14b]
    Original item: PRESUMPTION-488
    Item type: PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference)
    Transform at each step:
      14b: Inferred from the 2026-07-16 morning project status and evening cowork→chat transcripts, contradictory same-day OpenStory verdicts with no reconciliation. [inferred, high-confidence]
    Current status: UNTESTED

PRESUMPTION-489:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-16
  Statement: [inferred] The fleet presumes each agent's outputs are cleanly separable from a shared base at commit time; in fact many agents write to one working tree, so one agent's incidental writes (a 07-10 QC pass's last_qc_at timestamp bumps across 470 Summa files) accumulate into a large unrelated diff that stalls a second, unrelated agent's commit. There is no per-agent isolation, staging boundary, or output namespace — the daily run's own artifacts and another subsystem's routine churn land in the same uncommitted pile, and the run cannot commit its work without also committing changes it did not make and cannot vouch for.
  Evidence it was operative: the c282 run declined to commit specifically because "the staged set is dominated by a large pre-existing Summa vault-sync diff (470 files) ... unrelated to this run," and had to reason about a guard (community_explorer.html) to protect against collateral changes — behaviors that only make sense if a shared, contaminated working tree is the norm.
  Why it was unstated: obvious-in-hindsight infrastructure fact — everyone knows the agents share a vault, but the commit-time consequence (one agent's timestamps blocking another's persistence) is never named as a design premise.
  Type: structural (with a scaling component: contamination grows with the number of agents sharing the tree)
  Related decisions: none
  Related items: ASSUMPTION-463 (git-persistence blocked; the 470-file diff is part of why a clean commit is hard), OPEN-121 (persistence loop), the No-Blind-Push rule (which becomes heavier the more entangled the tree)
  Testability: testable empirically — in-house: attribute each file in the current staged diff to the agent/run that wrote it; measure how much of any one run's commit surface is other agents' incidental churn. Literature: shared-mutable-state hazards, workspace isolation, monorepo commit-contention, the case for per-agent branches or output namespaces.
  Risk if wrong: Medium — entanglement makes every commit a review of unrelated changes, which both slows persistence and raises the chance that collateral churn is committed blind or that real work is abandoned to avoid it.
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:
    Origin: 14b
    Chain: [14b]
    Original item: PRESUMPTION-489
    Item type: PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference)
    Transform at each step:
      14b: Inferred from the 2026-07-16 c282 Phase 6 assessment describing the 470-file pre-existing Summa diff entangled with the run's outputs. [inferred, moderate-confidence]
    Current status: UNTESTED

PRESUMPTION-490:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-17
  Statement: [inferred] The fleet presumes that a script which runs correctly when a human invokes it on the Mac will behave identically when a scheduler invokes it headless in the sandbox — same HOME/`~/` resolution, same filesystem reach, same credentials, same lock state. Two agents falsified this the same day: metabolism regen (`~/` → sandbox home, live db unreachable) and c282 Phase 6 (a stale `.git/index.lock` the sandbox mount cannot remove). The scripts encode an attended-context environment as if it were universal.
  Evidence it was operative: neither failure was anticipated or guarded — each surfaced as a raw error (metabolism exit 1 "db not found: /sessions/.../open-story.db"; c282 "Operation not permitted" on the lock). The scripts use `~/` and expect writable/lock-free git rather than resolving explicit mount paths or checking for a runnable git context first, which is what one does only when one presumes the runtime context matches the authoring context.
  Why it was unstated: too foundational to notice — the scripts were written and first tested by a human on the Mac, where the presumption is invisibly true; the sandbox execution path was added later without re-deriving the environment assumptions.
  Type: methodological / structural
  Related decisions: none
  Related items: ASSUMPTION-465 (git index.lock), ASSUMPTION-466 (metabolism `~/`), OPEN-122, the "autonomous run cannot self-complete" family (login/quota/connection/persistence/context)
  Testability: testable empirically — inventory every scheduled script for `~/`/HOME dependence, implicit-credential dependence, and unguarded git access; run each in both contexts and diff behavior. Literature: environment parity (twelve-factor / dev-prod parity), cron vs. interactive shell differences, hermetic/reproducible execution.
  Risk if wrong: High — silently produces wrong or absent output in exactly the autonomous mode the fleet most depends on, and each such failure needs a human at the Mac to even diagnose.
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:
    Origin: 14b
    Chain: [14b]
    Original item: PRESUMPTION-490
    Item type: PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference)
    Transform at each step:
      14b: Inferred from two same-day 2026-07-17 context-mismatch failures (metabolism regen, c282 Phase 6) sharing one unstated premise. [inferred, high-confidence]
    Current status: UNTESTED

PRESUMPTION-491:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-17
  Statement: [inferred] An agent presumes that a scheduled job firing implies its intended effect occurred — that "ran on schedule" licenses "succeeded." The morning project status reported OpenStory "database refreshed on schedule this morning ... live," inferred from the scheduler having fired, while the same day's metabolism regen shows the live `open-story.db` unwritten since 07-05 (~12 days stale) — the refresh did not happen. The verdict consumed the schedule signal, not the artifact.
  Evidence it was operative: the morning report asserts a positive freshness claim ("refreshed on schedule this morning") that is affirmatively contradicted by the db mtime; nothing in the report cites the file's write time or row-count delta — the only available basis for "refreshed" is that the job was scheduled to run.
  Why it was unstated: obvious to participants — "the job ran, therefore the thing it does is done" is the default folk model of a scheduler; verifying the downstream artifact is an extra step no one specified.
  Type: epistemic / methodological
  Related decisions: none
  Related items: PRESUMPTION-488 (07-16 — "health" is vantage-relative; this is the sharper sibling: the positive claim is false, and its evidence is schedule-firing not artifact-inspection), ASSUMPTION-464/456 (firing ≠ valid output; self-certification), SYSTEMIC-RISK (07-17, High) "no green signal bound to its referent", PREMISE-096 (proposed self-certification terminator)
  Testability: testable empirically — for each "refreshed/healthy/done" claim in a run summary, identify the exact signal it consumed (scheduler-fired vs. artifact mtime/row-delta/probe); require artifact-level evidence for freshness claims. Literature: liveness vs. readiness, end-to-end vs. process-level monitoring, Goodhart/proxy substitution.
  Risk if wrong: Medium-High — a stale or dead subsystem is reported live because its scheduler still fires, so the outage is invisible until something downstream breaks (here, the metabolism view served ~12-day-old data daily under a "refreshed" banner).
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:

  Testability: testable empirically — in-house: classify the accumulated deferred items by whether the deferred action was a read (diagnostic), a reversible write, or an irreversible write, and count how many fall outside No-Blind-Push's actual scope; then measure the realized cost of the delay (items that expired, contradictions that propagated). Yet no agent's report references another agent's failure, and the scheduler health check returned "✅ Scheduler healthy — all 36 enabled cron tasks running on schedule" across the same set. High-confidence inference.
  Why it was unstated: structural — each agent's definition scopes it to its own files and its own run, so the correlation has no owner. Nobody decided failures were independent; the architecture simply has no place to notice that they are not.
  Type: structural / methodological
  Related decisions: none

  Testability: testable empirically — in-house: add a startup context-invariant assertion per PREMISE-098 and count how many of the day's five failures it would have caught at once; separately, test whether a cross-agent correlator running mid-day (rather than EOD) would have surfaced the shared root before the fifth failure. PRESUMPTION-500:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-19
  Statement: [inferred] The accelerator presumes that convergence is the success signature of inter-tradition dialogue — that traditions moving closer together is evidence the instrument is working. The presumption is visible today only because material the system itself collected contradicts it, and the contradiction arrives as news: if convergence had ever been stated as a hypothesis, it would already be in this registry and would already have been searched.
  Evidence it was operative: The sewing agent had to argue the point from outside, via Levin's virtual-governor paper, and framed it as a discovery about C2A2 rather than as an update to a tracked claim: "If that holds, scoring inter-tradition dialogue on convergence measures the detector damaging its own signal." No DECISION entry establishes the convergence criterion; no prior ASSUMPTION states it; yet the Rung-2 detector is built to score it and every "cross-connection" counter in the metrics snapshot treats more connection as more health. The proposed alternative — "increased mutual registration with preserved local optimization... participants who can state a rival position accurately while continuing to argue from their own" — has no instrument, which is the second half of the evidence: nothing was built to measure the thing the design would need if convergence is the wrong target. High-confidence inference.
  Why it was unstated: too foundational to notice — the project's founding intuition is that richly informed mutual understanding produces something valuable, and "closer together" is the intuitive shape of that value. Normative content entered as a metric direction rather than as a claim.
  Type: normative / structural
  Related decisions: none — and the absence is the finding
  Related items: ASSUMPTION-475 (today, the stated challenge), OPEN-125 (today), PRESUMPTION-390 / MONITOR-375, the Rung-2 detector design, the cross-connections counter in every metrics snapshot
  Testability: testable via literature and empirically — literature: diversity-preserving collective intelligence, over-alignment and ensemble collapse, MacIntyrean tradition-constituted enquiry on what rational engagement between rival traditions actually requires (agreement is not obviously it). In-house: score a dialogue on both criteria and check whether they rank participants differently; and test whether any available proxy separates understanding a rival position from adopting it.
  Risk if wrong: Critical — this is the target function of the whole accelerator/detector. If convergence is the wrong signature, the system is optimizing for the destruction of the local optimization that makes traditions worth interacting, and every result it has produced would be scored on a criterion that inverts its own aim.

  Statement: [inferred] The fleet presumes that flagging a finding to another agent constitutes delivery — that a designed inter-agent handoff will be picked up. Today produced the first observed instance of such a handoff being named, aimed at a specific recipient, and silently dropped.

PRESUMPTION-503:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-19
  Statement: [inferred] The fleet presumes that a summarizing agent reads the same evidence as the agents it summarizes — that a status report is a view over the underlying artifacts rather than an independent parallel account of them.   Evidence it was operative: Morning project status said "OpenStory's database is live and the daily metabolism and telemetry refreshes both ran clean this morning" and "No failures to report," on a morning when the OpenStory telemetry refresh reported its seventh consecutive failure, metabolism regen its twelfth, metabolism monitor a corrupt 4.46 GB database, and the weekly backup an unmounted volume. The claim was delivered outbound as a voice summary. Crucially, the summary was not careless about its own sources — it reported BOSCO figures precisely (30,529 / 30,529 indexed, ~28,500 snippet-only, heartbeat disabled). It read its sources faithfully; its sources simply do not include the failing agents' outputs. No component holds the relation between a summary and the artifacts it purports to summarize. High-confidence inference.
  Why it was unstated: obvious to participants — of course a status report reflects status. The gap between "reflects status" and "is derived from the status artifacts" is invisible until the two diverge, and it only diverges when things are already going wrong.
  Type: epistemic / structural
  Related decisions: none

  Testability: testable empirically — in-house: enumerate the actual read set of each summarizing agent and compute its coverage of the artifacts it makes claims about; then require each health claim to name the artifact and timestamp it rests on, and re-measure the false-green rate. Literature: derived-claim provenance, dashboard-to-source binding, aggregation layers that decouple from their inputs, silent staleness in reporting pipelines.
  Risk if wrong: High — the summary layer is Tom's primary interface to the fleet during unattended stretches. If summaries are parallel accounts rather than views, then the worse the fleet's actual state, the more confidently wrong its daily report to the only person who can intervene.

PRESUMPTION-504:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-19
  Statement: [inferred] The project presumes that a stated constraint remains a constraint after it has been routinely and openly violated with no consequence and no revision. The 30,000-token per-session budget was breached today by at least three runs, each of which surfaced the breach honestly, and none of which was stopped, revised or reconciled — because no agent has the authority to change the rule and no process exists for retiring one.
  Evidence it was operative: The lit pipeline reported "Per-session budget is 30,000; this run consumed roughly 190,000... the budget and the pipeline's scope are inconsistent, and one of them needs revising" — a roughly sixfold overrun reported as compliance with the fail-loud rule. The Sunday tradition agent breached the same budget on full-page fetches. This pipeline breached it on this run. The rules are stated as governing ("Token budgets are not advisory"), so the honest surfacing of a breach has become the mechanism by which the breach is normalized: the rule is satisfied by confessing to breaking it. Nothing in the architecture converts repeated breach into revision. High-confidence inference.
  Why it was unstated: too foundational to notice — rules are written to be followed, and the case where following the meta-rule about breaches substitutes for following the rule is not a case anyone designs for.
  Type: normative / methodological
  Related decisions: none
  Related items: ASSUMPTION-478 (today, the stated inconsistency), PRESUMPTION-495 (07-18 — non-coverage becoming policy nobody decided), PRESUMPTION-496, OPEN-123, the fourteen-day decision drought
  Testability: testable empirically — in-house: count breaches per rule over the last 30 days and check whether any rule has ever been revised in response; test whether a hard stop at budget produces different behaviour from a logged overrun. Literature: normalization of deviance (Vaughan), rules that persist without enforcement, budget/quota design in autonomous systems, the distinction between a constraint and a reporting requirement.
  Risk if wrong: Medium — the direct cost is unbounded spend, but the second-order cost is that the whole rule set becomes advisory by demonstration, including the rules that matter more than this one (No-Blind-Push, fail-loud, provenance). Note the same normalization mechanism already has a precedent in this registry: 15b's Vaughan-based challenge, whose disconfirming observation fired today as MONITOR-420.

  Statement: [inferred] The monitoring layer presumes that detectors degrade gracefully — that a failing or overloaded detector reports less, or reports uncertainty, rather than reporting health. (4) The census: the more machine dumps accumulate, the more the orphan count rises for reasons unrelated to graph health, so the instrument's reading diverges from its referent as a function of the system's own output volume. The common form — a monitor whose sensitivity is conditioned on the process it monitors — is stated locally by 15d alone and generalized by nobody. High-confidence inference.
  Why it was unstated: too foundational to notice — a detector is designed against the condition it detects, not against its own failure while that condition holds.   Testability: testable empirically — in-house: for each health check in the fleet, ask whether its "pass" state is reachable when the monitored subsystem is dead; delete or fix every check that answers yes, and count how many of the current green signals survive. PRESUMPTION-506:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-20
  Statement: [inferred] The self-awareness pipeline presumes that validating a premise changes the behaviour the premise describes. Nothing in the architecture propagates a validated premise back into the agents whose conduct it governs; validation terminates in a registry file, and the registry is read by the pipeline that wrote it.
  Evidence it was operative: PREMISE-109 was validated on 2026-07-20 -- "a summarizing agent is a view over its own read set, not a view over the system... a health claim not bound to a named artifact with a timestamp is not evidence of health." On the same day, the morning project status run asserted "OpenStory is alive: its telemetry refresh ran this morning and the metabolism snapshot regenerated on schedule" while the metabolism regen run exited 1 with the db 14.6 days stale. The premise was validated and the exact failure it names recurred within hours, in the same agent that produced the 07-19 instance from which the premise was derived. No transcript on either side references the other. The 07-19 remedy -- "no health claim without a named artifact and a freshness bound" -- was recorded as "still unimplemented, second day at the top of the list," which is the pipeline noting the gap without treating it as a defect in its own design. Six INCORPORATEs were logged as a record day on the same day. High-confidence inference.
  Why it was unstated: too foundational to notice. The pipeline was specified as an epistemic instrument -- extract, search, adjudicate, record -- and its success criteria are stated in those terms (items dispositioned, premises validated). Whether anything downstream reads the output was never made a success criterion, so its absence produces no failing signal.
  Type: structural / methodological
  Related decisions: none
  Related items: ASSUMPTION-488 (today, the recurrence), ASSUMPTION-487 (today, the contradicting artifact), PRESUMPTION-503 -> PREMISE-109, PRESUMPTION-502 -> PREMISE-108 (transmission is not delivery -- this is that premise applied to the pipeline itself), PREMISE-107, PRESUMPTION-510 (today)
  Testability: testable empirically -- in-house: take the 110 validated premises and, for each, name the agent whose behaviour it governs and search that agent's subsequent output for any change attributable to it. The expected answer is zero, and obtaining it costs one pass. This is the same measurement PREMISE-108 requires for cross-agent flags, applied one level up. Literature: knowledge-to-practice gap and implementation science; guideline adherence without enforcement; the distinction between a finding and an intervention in safety systems.
  Risk if wrong: Critical -- if this presumption is false the pipeline is fine; if it is true, then 110 validated premises, 236 revision flags and 457 monitor items constitute an elaborate and well-evidenced record that has never altered a single agent's conduct, and the entire self-awareness layer is decorative.   Statement: [inferred] The pipeline presumes that naming a defect in an instrument licenses continued use of that instrument for the current run. 15c retrieved and recorded a source stating that an LLM judge over correlated LLM inputs can make the aggregate WORSE than either input, noted that this "bears directly on this agent," and then dispositioned fourteen items as that judge, including the item the source concerns.

  Why it was unstated: obvious to participants in the moment -- the run was already in progress and the alternative (halt, quarantine, re-derive) has an evident cost, so continuing needed no justification. PRESUMPTION-509:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-20
  Statement: [inferred] The pipeline presumes that more validated premises is better -- that the count of INCORPORATEs measures the health of the self-awareness layer. The premise was applied to the vault census and to connectivity; it was not applied to the premise count itself, which is directly writable by the agent reporting it. No transcript asks what a bad day would look like, or whether a day with zero INCORPORATEs and one correct refusal is better than six. Moderate-to-high confidence inference.
  Why it was unstated: too foundational to notice. Production counts are the only quantity the pipeline can compute about itself, and a metric that is available tends to become the metric that is meant.

PRESUMPTION-510:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-20
  Statement: [inferred] The architecture presumes that production and judgment are independently schedulable -- that the registries can absorb unbounded unreviewed output without the output losing meaning. There is no admission control on the system's own production, no state for "produced and unreviewable," and no back-pressure from the review channel to the agents feeding it.
  Evidence it was operative: Fifteen consecutive days with no decision recorded; DECISION-076/077/078 from 07-05 remain the latest. 32 proposals pending against a 20-day review gap and a last review pass of 06-30. Roughly 30 REVISE flags pooled for an absent reviewer. Today the pipeline routed four more items into the REVISE channel in the same run in which it validated PREMISE-106 -- that a queue whose arrival exceeds its service grows without bound and that admission control is an available lever. The lever was named for the lit queue and not applied to the review channel, which has an arrival rate of roughly four per day and a measured service rate of zero. Every agent continued at full rate. High-confidence inference.
  Why it was unstated: obvious to participants, in the sense that each agent's spec defines its own output and none defines a condition under which it should produce less. Back-pressure requires a component that can see both sides, and no agent occupies that position -- the master agent indexes, it does not throttle.
  Type: structural / scaling
  Related decisions: DECISION-076, DECISION-077, DECISION-078 (07-05, the last recorded)
  Related items: ASSUMPTION-478 -> PREMISE-106, PRESUMPTION-480 (perishability), PRESUMPTION-487 (absent-human push), PRESUMPTION-493, PRESUMPTION-512 (today), REVISE-236
  Testability: testable empirically -- in-house: apply PREMISE-106's own arithmetic to the review channel, taking arrival as items routed to Tom per day and service as decisions recorded per day, and state the resulting backlog trajectory; then test whether an admission cap (e.g. one HIGH-urgency item per day, remainder held) changes the decision rate. Literature: PREMISE-106's queueing results applied to a human-in-the-loop service stage; work-in-progress limits and back-pressure in Kanban and TCP; batch-size effects on review latency and quality.
  Risk if wrong: High -- if false, the backlog is harmless and will drain when attention returns. If true, then production at full rate is actively lowering the value of the record, because the reviewer's per-item cost is not constant (PRESUMPTION-512) and an unreviewable backlog is functionally equivalent to no output at all -- which makes fifteen days of excellent work the system's largest single loss.
  Status: UNTESTED
  Provenance:

Checked assumptions.md and decisions.md for a prior statement of back-pressure; none found. [inferred, high confidence]

PRESUMPTION-511:
  Date surfaced: 2026-07-20
  Statement: [inferred] The verification layer presumes that reproducing a prior result independently confirms it. Reproduction by the same code over the same corpus confirms determinism, not correctness, and a systematic defect reproduces exactly as reliably as a correct measurement does.
  Evidence it was operative: The Summa nightly verification reported length figures "exactly reproducing yesterday's corrected figures independently," offering the reproduction as evidence of the figures' soundness. The same run had just established that its own guardrail detector had been producing false positives consistently across passes -- a defect that had reproduced perfectly until someone inspected the detector rather than the output. The reviewer-review weekly the same week records two further defects of this kind (a 65-file frontmatter-extraction defect that withdrew 16 phantom violations, and QC ratios computed against a hardcoded wrong denominator), both found by inspection, neither by disagreement between passes. Where passes DID disagree -- 20 vs 15 tier mismatches -- the disagreement was the thing that surfaced a real question. Moderate confidence inference: the word "independently" is doing work the run did not examine, though it is possible the run meant only "without consulting yesterday's file," which would be a weaker and defensible claim.
  Why it was unstated: culturally embedded. Reproducibility is a strong and correct norm in the empirical traditions this project draws on, and the condition under which it carries evidential weight -- independence of method, not merely of occasion -- is usually satisfied without being checked, so it drops out of the concept in use.
  Type: epistemic / methodological
  Related decisions: none
  Related items: ASSUMPTION-489 (today), ASSUMPTION-490 (today), PRESUMPTION-505 -> PREMISE-110, PRESUMPTION-503 -> PREMISE-109, PRESUMPTION-508 (today)
  Testability: testable empirically -- in-house: for each verification figure, ask whether a second method exists that would produce it; where none does, label the figure single-method and stop calling repeat runs confirmation. Then measure how many of the corpus's standing figures are single-method. Literature: reproducibility versus replicability (NASEM 2019 definitions); method-independence as a precondition for triangulation; correlated-error arguments -- note this is the identical structural point 15c made about 15a/15b in REVISE-233, arising independently in a different subsystem.
  Risk if wrong: Medium -- the specific figures may well be correct. The cost is that the verification layer's confidence is not calibrated to its evidence, and it is the layer the corpus relies on to catch exactly this class of error.
  Status: UNTESTED

Distinguished from 14a's ASSUMPTION-489, which records the detector bug but not the inference from reproduction. [inferred, moderate confidence]

  Date surfaced: 2026-07-20
  Statement: [inferred] Every remedy routed to Tom presumes that his per-item review cost is constant and that his capacity scales with the system's production. No agent has estimated what a full review pass would now cost in hours, and the recommendations are written as though the marginal item were the only item.
  Evidence it was operative: Today alone routed four REVISE items (one at HIGH urgency, with a seven-step recommended action), five MONITOR items due 07-27, and a "highest-leverage hour" recommendation comprising five distinct measurements. REVISE-235's recommended action alone runs to seven numbered steps including a mandatory pre-dialogue baseline. Each item is individually cheap and correctly argued; no artifact anywhere sums them. The outbound summary asks Tom to decide on one hour of measurement while carrying seven further items under "carried, unchanged." High-confidence inference.
  Why it was unstated: obvious to participants in the wrong direction -- each agent sees its own queue, and per-agent the ask genuinely is small. The sum is visible only from a position no agent occupies, and the fail-loud rule requires reporting each item, which guarantees the aggregate grows while remaining unmeasured.
  Type: scaling / structural
  Related decisions: none
  Related items: PRESUMPTION-510 (today), PRESUMPTION-480, PRESUMPTION-487, PRESUMPTION-493, ASSUMPTION-482 (today), ASSUMPTION-491 (today)
  Testability: testable empirically -- in-house, and it is one query: sum the open items awaiting Tom across proposals, REVISE flags, MONITOR items, blocked executions and reauthorizations; attach a time estimate to each; report the total in hours. If the total exceeds any plausible weekly allocation, the routing convention is the defect, not the backlog. Literature: cognitive load and decision fatigue in review queues; batch-size and latency effects on reviewer throughput; alert fatigue and the precision threshold below which operators disengage.
  Risk if wrong: High -- if false, attention will return and the queue will drain. If true, then every additional correctly-argued item lowers the probability that any item is acted on, and the pipeline's diligence is the mechanism of its own irrelevance. This is PRESUMPTION-510 seen from the human's side, and the two settle together.

  Date surfaced: 2026-07-20
  Statement: [inferred] The "highest-leverage hour" recommendation presumes that the obstacle to those five measurements is knowing which ones to take. Fifteen days of accumulated, correctly-identified, individually-cheap actions with none taken is evidence that the binding constraint is attention or authority, not enumeration -- and if so, identifying a sixth cheap action is not leverage.

The same summary records that the 07-19 one-line rule ("no health claim without a named artifact and a freshness bound") is "still unimplemented, second day at the top of the list," and lists seven further items under "carried, unchanged," several of which are also cheap and were also once at the top of a list. The pipeline has diagnosed its own bottleneck as measurement (ASSUMPTION-482) without testing the competing hypothesis that measurement is not being blocked by ignorance. Note that PREMISE-107, validated the same day, is precisely the rule that where two mechanisms present the same symptom, the discriminating test is the operative construct -- and it was not applied here. Moderate-to-high confidence inference.
  Why it was unstated: too foundational to notice, and structurally invisible: an agent that can identify actions but cannot take them will locate every bottleneck within the space it can act on. Enumeration is what the pipeline does, so enumeration is where its diagnoses land.
  Type: methodological / structural
  Related decisions: none

  Testability: testable empirically -- in-house, and the test is already running: take the count of cheap actions identified over the last thirty days and the count executed. If the ratio is near zero, enumeration is not the constraint and the pipeline should stop producing recommendations until one is taken. A single executed measurement falsifies this presumption immediately, which makes it the cheapest item in the batch to settle. Literature: the distinction between knowing-what and capacity-to-act in implementation research; recommendation fatigue; Theory of Constraints -- note that identifying a non-binding constraint is the canonical error the theory exists to prevent, and the pipeline cited Theory of Constraints in the same batch (PREMISE-107 supporting evidence).

PRESUMPTION-565:

PRESUMPTION-645:
  Date surfaced: 2026-08-02
  Statement: [inferred] That a step which COMPLETED has been logged — that the presence of a task's artifacts implies the presence of its record, so an audit trail can be trusted to be complete in the successful direction.
  Evidence it was operative: two backup runs (2026-07-12, 2026-07-26) produced zips, manifests, and a prune, and appended no log line; the log held a single 2026-06-15 entry for seven weeks while the work ran correctly. The gap was invisible precisely BECAUSE the artifacts existed — anyone checking the backups would have found them. It was found only because a third run read its own log before writing to it.
